verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; STOP invoked on one confirmed memory-safety defect class (uninitialised read / invalid free on an allocation-failure path) and repaired in this batch; one unsafe-contract understatement repaired; targeted Miri control added and run under both aliasing models.
scope: Per-file contract audit of the SLH-DSA key management and signature provider rows, the SM2 asymmetric-cipher and signature rows, the provider method-store/cache bridges, the shared provider utility helpers (cipher, digest, MAC context, memdup), the RFC 3492 punycode decoder and the QUIC variable-length integer codec. All eight entries were the head of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt; none was deferred.

defects.class: uninitialised read / invalid free on an allocation-failure path
defects.description: Both AlgorithmIdentifier builders declared the packet as MaybeUninit::<Wpacket>::uninit() and then called WPACKET_cleanup unconditionally, mirroring the authority. WPACKET_init_der can refuse for two reasons: a bad argument (null buffer or zero length), which returns before writing anything, and a failed WPACKET_SUB allocation inside wpacket_intern_init_len, which has written curr/written but not subs. WPACKET_cleanup reads (*pkt).subs, so on that allocation-failure arm the Rust read an uninitialised *mut WpacketSub and could dereference or free a garbage pointer (the C authority has the same defect). The packet is now core::mem::zeroed::<Wpacket>() with a SAFETY: note; Wpacket is a #[repr(C)] record of raw pointers, size_t values and one unsigned int bitfield, so all-zero is a valid value and leaves an empty sub-packet chain. WPACKET_init_der writes every field on success, so no reachable success-path behaviour changes. A test-only negative control drives the argument refusal into the same early-return state and cleans up the zeroed packet.

ossl_quic_vlint_decode's # Safety contract read '`v` is NULL or writable', but the body writes *v unconditionally on success (the authority dereferences it without a NULL test). A caller obeying the stated contract could therefore cause UB through a documented precondition. The contract now requires v to be non-NULL and writable and the inline SAFETY: note says the caller's contract is the only guard. No code changed.

class_findings_outside_batch.summary: The M70-D1 pattern (cleanup of a non-zeroed packet after a possibly-refused WPACKET initialisation) remains in six other source files. It is a shared-callee defect: wpacket_intern_init_len allocates the first WPACKET_SUB after writing curr/written but without clearing subs on failure.

class_findings_outside_batch.recommended_repair: Clear (*pkt).subs in wpacket_intern_init_len before OwnedSub::zalloc, so every initialiser that reaches it leaves a cleanable packet on refusal. That is a change to a shared ownership mechanism and requires its own BOUNDARY sweep (independent caller audit, targeted Miri, negative control) rather than being folded into this per-file batch.

retained_obligations: The provider dispatch callbacks receive borrowed raw pointers; key and context lifetimes are the EVP caller's obligation.
ProvSlhDsaCtx.alg is a borrowed static algorithm-name literal supplied by this file's own MAKE_SIGNATURE_FUNCTIONS expansion; the newctx dispatch contract is the guard.
ProvSlhDsaCtx.key and ProvSm2Ctx.key / ProvSm2SigCtx.ec are borrowed EVP/EC objects carrying their own reference; the destructor body releases exactly that reference.
ProvSlhDsaCtx and SlhDsaGenCtx destructors rely on the OB-3 zero-validity contract, covered by the existing zero_state_sweep controls.
The method-store slots in provider/stores.rs hold objects context_init built and released once; the bridge's typed cast is valid only under that slot invariant.
slh_dsa_signverify_msg_init replaces ctx->hash_ctx without releasing a previous one when an init with a key is repeated: the authority's own leak, not UB, intentionally preserved.

secret_bearing_buffers: src/provider/slh_dsa_kmgmt.rs SlhDsaGenCtx.entropy: the caller-supplied seed; cleansed by SlhDsaGenCtx::destroy_body on gen_cleanup and on the gen_init failure path, and the buffer is the authority's own OPENSSL_zalloc block.

src/provider/slh_dsa_kmgmt.rs export params: the private-key octet-string copy made by OSSL_PARAM_BLD is cleansed for every entry (also the public one) before OSSL_PARAM_free, matching the authority's loop.

src/provider/slh_dsa_sig.rs ProvSlhDsaCtx.add_random: the caller's test entropy; cleansed in ProvSlhDsaCtx::destroy_body (freectx and the newctx/dupctx failure paths) and never before the signature that consumes it.

src/provider/slh_dsa_sig.rs slh_dsa_sign add_rand: the provider-drawn one-time randomness; cleansed after the sign when and only when the provider drew it (the authority's own rule). The caller's test-entropy buffer is borrowed and not cleansed by this unit.
src/provider/slh_dsa_sig.rs context_string: public context metadata, not cleansed (authority parity).
src/provider/slh_dsa_sig.rs, slh_dsa_kmgmt.rs private key: borrowed through EVP_PKEY and released by its owner, never copied by these units.
src/provider/sm2_enc.rs, src/provider/sm2_sig.rs private key: borrowed EC_KEY with its own reference; released through EC_KEY_free; B19's BIGNUM cleansing covers the key components.
src/provider/sm2_sig.rs id (SM2 distid): public user identity, released plainly through the authority's free sites; propq is public metadata.
src/provider/sm2_sig.rs digest arrays: the public Z||message digest, not secret-bearing.

src/provider/util.rs ossl_prov_memdup: copies a caller's bucket (its KDF callers copy secret material); the caller's own destructor performs the cleanse, as in the authority. The helper stores no state.
src/provider/stores.rs, src/punycode.rs, src/quic_vlint.rs: no secret-bearing storage.

boundary_control.name: provider::slh_dsa_sig::tests::a_refused_der_init_leaves_a_cleanable_packet
boundary_control.reason: The repaired branch is only reachable through WPACKET_init_der's node-allocation refusal, and no allocator-injection harness exists for it. The control drives the argument refusal, which takes the same early-return path out of the initialiser, and then runs WPACKET_cleanup on the image the repair establishes; under Miri an uninitialised subs read is an error, so a regression to MaybeUninit fails the control rather than passing silently.
